## The study

This study asks whether screening US deceased kidney donors for serum cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) is worth its cost, using a decision-analytic cost-effectiveness model that compares universal donor screening with no routine screening. [The decision model](model_structure.qmd) explains how.

The analysis is preliminary and not for citation. The current results are on the [Results](results_base_case.qmd) pages; they come from the model as it now stands, which does not yet match every part of the analysis plan.

-   **Vagish Hemmige** (investigator, model and this repository)

Scientific decisions are made by Vagish Hemmige, and open ones are listed in the analysis plan's [open decisions](analysis-plan.qmd#14-open-decisions).

## This repository

The analysis is written as scripts run in order by `R/main.R`. It uses no data set: every model input is a value from the published literature, guidelines or registry reports, entered in `R/setup.R` and summarized with its sources on the [Evidence base for parameters](../references/literature-review.md) page. An input that rests on unpublished data is described as "source to be documented" until it can be cited.

Contributions follow the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](agents.qmd); known issues and gaps between the code and the plan are tracked in [`TODO.md`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Cryptococcus-donor-screening-CEA/blob/master/TODO.md).

## How this website was created

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from the analysis scripts themselves. Each code page imports the labelled sections of its script from `R/` and shows them with an explanation; the site never runs the model. The results pages read the files the model saved in `output/` and `figures/`, and a GitHub Actions workflow renders and publishes the site on every change to `master`.

The repository is maintained with the [R Analysis Workflow](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/r-analysis-workflow) plugin for AI coding assistants, written by Vagish Hemmige. The plugin provides the repository layout, the conventions for the analysis plan and `AGENTS.md`, and the format of these pages. AI assistants drafted code, documentation and suggestions under the rules in `AGENTS.md`: they never handle unpublished material, and every scientific decision is made by the investigator.

Four documents describe the project. In short: the plan is the scientific intent, the architecture is the workflow as implemented, and `AGENTS.md` holds the rules for working together.

-   [**Analysis plan**](analysis-plan.qmd): *what the analysis is meant to do, and why.* The comparators, population, unit of analysis, perspective, model structure, inputs, sensitivity analyses, and the open decisions. Code implements it and does not redefine it.
-   [**Architecture**](architecture.qmd): *how the code does it.* The scripts, the order they run in, what each needs and produces, and how data flow between them.
-   [**AGENTS.md**](agents.qmd): *how people and AI assistants work on the project.* Rules for unpublished material, coding, checks, proposing changes and getting a person's approval.
-   [**Repository blueprint**](repository-blueprint.qmd): *the layout every project of this kind starts from*, which the architecture document then describes as built.

## Pages

-   [**Clinical background**](background.qmd): donor-derived cryptococcosis in kidney transplantation, and why donor screening is debated.
-   [**Cost-effectiveness analysis for clinicians**](cea_primer.qmd): costs, QALYs, the ICER and net monetary benefit, in general terms.
-   [**Sensitivity analyses explained**](uncertainty_methods.qmd): scenario, one-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses, and how to read their figures.
-   [**The decision model**](model_structure.qmd): the tree, its pathways, the unit of analysis and the model's known limitations.
-   [**How the inputs are chosen**](model_inputs.qmd): best estimates, the distributions that describe their uncertainty, and the parameter table.
-   [**Evidence base for parameters**](../references/literature-review.md): the published evidence for every input, compared with the values the model uses.
-   [**Setup and parameters**](setup.qmd): packages, every model parameter, the willingness-to-pay threshold, the seed and the number of simulations.
-   [**Functions**](functions.qmd): the functions that compute and draw the decision tree.
-   [**Base-case tree**](base_case_tree.qmd): runs the tree at base-case values and saves its tables and figures.
-   [**Scenario trees**](scenario_trees.qmd): reruns the tree under four alternative sets of assumptions.
-   [**Sensitivity analyses**](sensitivity_analyses.qmd): the one-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses.
-   [**Base case**](results_base_case.qmd), [**Scenario analyses**](results_scenarios.qmd), [**One-way sensitivity (tornado)**](results_tornado.qmd) and [**Probabilistic sensitivity**](results_psa.qmd): the results, read from the saved outputs.
